title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous pages): for a k-module M, Grothendieck uses the functor V(M): A ↦ Hom_k(M, A), the 'generic' dual. A coalgebra structure Δ: M → M⊗M is encoded as a natural bilinear law of composition on V(M), which makes V(M) a functor in (non-unital) algebras, the 'algèbre générique'. A grading M = ⊕_{α∈Z} M_α by a set Z corresponds to a product decomposition V(M) = ∏ V(M_α). When Z is an abelian group, the grading is the same as an action of the diagonalizable group G = D(Z) = Spec k[Z], with G(A) = Hom(Z, A^*). This is the standard SGA3 dictionary.

This page:
(1) A coalgebra Δ on M is compatible with the grading if it respects the total grading, i.e. Δ(M_n) ⊂ Σ_{i+j=n} M_i⊗M_j. Equivalently, the law on V(M) comes from maps V(M_i)×V(M_j) → V(M_{i+j}). The interlinear notes rename V(M_i) as V(M)^i, so this reads as a graded multiplication V(M)^i × V(M)^j → V(M)^{i+j}. Equivalently again, the multiplication of V(M) (resp. the comultiplication of M) is G-equivariant.
(2) The left margin says Δ amounts to giving its components Δ_n: M_n → Σ_{i+j=n} M_i⊗M_j, dually ∏_{i+j=n} V(M_i)×V(M_j) → V(M_n).
(3) The NB treats 'true' families or sheaves of modules indexed by i, where M is not literally a direct sum. There one gives the individual components Δ^{(i,j)}: M_{i+j} → M_i⊗M_j and must impose a finiteness condition, so that Δ(x) has only finitely many nonzero components and lands in the direct sum.
(4) Homomorphisms of (graded) coalgebras correspond to homomorphisms of the associated commutative (graded) algebra functors.
(5) Toward sign rules: given a homomorphism Z → Z/2Z, equivalently by Cartier duality μ_2 → G, the Z-grading induces a Z/2-grading on M and on V(M). The next page then defines anticommutative and alternating coalgebras as those whose generic algebra V(M) = V(M)^even × V(M)^odd is graded-commutative, resp. alternating.

Purpose: to set up a functorial 'dual' language (coalgebras ↔ algebra-valued functors) for graded, divided-power and anticommutative structures. This is groundwork for the divided-power de Rham complex of the 1976 IHÉS lecture.
errors: No substantive error. Implicitly the law of composition on V(M) must be required to be bilinear (natural in A); otherwise natural maps V(M)×V(M)→V(M) correspond to maps into Sym(M)⊗Sym(M) rather than M⊗M. Grothendieck clearly means bilinear laws.

The equivalence 'grading-compatible ⇔ G-equivariant' is correct for G = D(Z) diagonalizable (SGA3 I 4.7.3). The NB rightly flags that a finiteness condition is needed when only the components Δ^{(i,j)} are given.

ideas.what: Coalgebra structure on M ↔ (bilinear) algebra structure on the functor V(M)=Hom(M,-) ('generic algebra')
ideas.modern_name: Linear duality between coalgebras and algebra-valued functors / formal schemes (Cartier duality style)
ideas.where_published: Related functor-of-points formalism in SGA3 Exp. I; not this exact formulation

ideas.what: Parity for sign rules obtained from a homomorphism Z→Z/2, i.e. μ_2→G
ideas.modern_name: Parity via a central μ_2→G, as in super-Tannakian pairs (G, ε)

missed.claim: Grothendieck encodes the Koszul sign convention for graded-commutative (co)algebras by a homomorphism μ_2 → G into the grading group G = D(Z). This is formally the device later central in Deligne's super-Tannakian theory, where a pair (G, ε) has ε: μ_2 → G determining parity. It is a small, unpublished anticipation, though the idea that parity comes from a μ_2-action is fairly natural.
missed.quote: Conditions d'anticommutativité, lorsqu'on dispose d'un hom Z → Z/2Z (i.e. μ_2 → G) qui permet de [déduire de] la graduation donnée une graduation à degrés dans Z/2Z, idem pour V(M).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck framing sign rules group-theoretically (via μ_2 → G) around 1976, before Deligne's systematic use of (G, ε). Mathematical content is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine foundational bookkeeping: graded coalgebras via the dual functor V(M), and gradings as D(Z)-actions (SGA3). The only mildly notable point is encoding parity through μ_2 → G, which anticipates Deligne's (G, ε) formalism. That is natural enough not to be surprising.
transcription_corrections: The labels under 'V(M_i) × V(M_j) → V(M_{i+j})' read 'V(M)^i   V(M)^j   V(M)^{i+j}' (renaming V(M_i) as V(M)^i), not 'V^i(M)^i [?] V^j(M_j)'.

The NB reads roughly: 'NB dans le cas de vrais "faisceaux de modules indexés par i", au lieu des Δ il suffit de se donner des Δ^{(i,j)}: M_{i+j} → M_i⊗M_j, et de ... condition de finitude'; its second line is 'V(M)^i × V(M)^j → V(M)^{i+j} ...'.

'Bien sûr, les' is followed by an omitted line, presumably 'hom. de coalgèbres (resp. de coalgèbres graduées) correspondent aux hom des O-Alg. commutatives (éventuellement graduées)'; 'O_n-Alg' is uncertain.
Last lines: 'qui permet de déduire de la graduation donnée de M une graduation à degrés dans Z/2Z, idem pour V(M)'.
'Il revient aussi au même de dire que la multiplication dans V(M) (resp. la comultiplication dans M) commute à l'action de G'.
